One blocker, from this card's own What #2 / Done-when #2:

**B1 — the gate only recognises a leak at `KB_ROOT` itself or inside another `kb-<n>-<k>` checkout; any other cwd still trusts the env** (`attemptIdentity`, src/model.js ~604: `if (!wt && !atRoot) return { n, k, source: 'env' }`). Reproduced: with this session's leaked `KB_TASK=146`, from `.claude/worktrees/review-152` the PR's pretool hook denies `for x in 1; do …; done` byte-identically to main, with no stderr line, and `whichAttempt()` answers `{146,1,env}` — so the Stop hook there would `writeSession` the operator's id back onto #146 attempt 1 (src/hook.js ~207 overwrites regardless of outcome), undoing the repair. Same hole across repos: a pipao-v2 session hosted by the poisoned daemon carries `KB_ROOT=…/harness-kanban-board`, cwd = pipao root → env trusted → pipao's hooks act as worker 146 on pipao's board. Poisoned daemons persist until restarted (six processes on this host right now), so "makes the next leak harmless" currently holds only at the board root. Fix: for a profile whose workspace is a worktree and with `KB_ROOT` set, the worker's root is deterministic — `path.join(KB_ROOT, worktreePath('kb-<n>-<k>'))` (`ensureWorktree`, src/board.js ~144; Claude's `--worktree` uses the same directory) — treat any other cwd as the leak, print the one stderr line, answer null. Apply the same rule in `checkEnvLeak` (src/doctor.js ~421), which today also reports nothing from a review worktree. Add the two tests: review-worktree cwd and foreign-repo cwd both → leak.

Also, while you are in there:
- S1: `docs/harnesses.md` says a session "plainly not sitting in the worktree of" its task falls back — true only after B1; align the prose (the wiki page already states the narrower rule, update it too).
- S2: `jobSessionUpdate` (src/jobs.js ~84) now overwrites whenever the job record's session differs, which includes the legitimate `claude --resume` case the old test guarded, and clears `total_cost_usd/num_turns/duration_ms`. Acceptable (logged in the tick, only open non-manual attempts on this host) — say so in the PR body rather than only "a hook stamp".
- N1: `atRoot` compares `path.resolve` strings — on Windows a drive-letter case mismatch defeats it; `fs.realpathSync` or case-folding on win32.
- N3: `preToolHook` re-reads `process.env.KB_PROFILE/KB_ROOT` after the gate instead of the identity it just computed.

results.summary: A `claude --bg` launch now carries no KB_* at all, and a hook that finds a KB_TASK its checkout contradicts stands aside. Four parts. (1) src/dispatch.js: a `mode: "claude-bg"` spawn gets `scrubKbEnv(process.env)` — every KB_* key removed — because a launch that finds no session daemon starts one and the daemon keeps that environment for life; it reaches no worker there anyway (#125), and Claude Code 2.1.x has no flag that hands env to the session instead (checked against `claude --help`). Every other mode is untouched: for a child process the env is the only identity there is and it dies with the process. (2) `attemptIdentity` (src/model.js) reconciles the environment with the checkout, and `whichAttempt` (src/hook.js) uses it: an env naming a task whose worktree this plainly is not is dropped, the checkout answers if it can, one line to stderr. Judged only on evidence (cwd is KB_ROOT, or a kb-<n>-<k> naming another attempt) and only for a profile whose worker hkb knows the location of (`worksInWorktree`: mode claude-bg or workspace worktree) — claude-p and claude-action are deliberately excluded, since neither can leak and where claude-p's hooks run is the harness's business. preToolHook now gates on `source === 'env'`. (3) `jobSessionUpdate` (src/jobs.js): when the job the tick matched to an OPEN attempt names a different session than the row, the job wins and the row is rewritten, clearing the fields the job cannot name so a corrected id never sits beside the replaced transcript; the tick logs the id it replaced. It cannot overwrite a verb's own stamp, because a verb closes the row it stamps and the tick only sees open attempts. (4) `checkEnvLeak`/`daemonsWithKbEnv` (src/doctor.js): a `worker environment` warning when doctor's own shell wears a contradicted identity, naming the daemon pids on Linux from /proc/<pid>/environ. NEXT WORKER, READ THIS: two tests in test/jobs.test.js changed contract (#137's "a row a terminal verb has stamped is byte-identical after a tick" no longer holds for a row naming a different session) — both rewritten with the reasoning. #146 attempt 1 was repaired to session 60f4948c-67d7-47dc-b554-afa3804d9618 by applying jobSessionUpdate once to the job id the row already carried: its attempt was already closed, so no tick will ever reach it. Its stale marker file at <board root>/.kanban/sessions/146-1 still holds the operator's session id; harmless (the attempt is closed and the hook now stands aside at the board root), but delete it if it ever matters. Daemons started before this fix keep their inherited KB_* until restarted — `hkb doctor` found six on this host and names their pids.

B1: `attemptIdentity` (src/model.js) had a `if (!wt && !atRoot) return { n, k, source: 'env' }` branch that trusted the environment from ANY cwd that wasn't the board root or a mismatched kb-<n>-<k> checkout — a review worktree, or a session a poisoned daemon went on to host for an unrelated repo, both read as agreement. Fixed so only a `kb-<n>-<k>` checkout naming this exact task and attempt counts as evidence for the environment; everything else (board root, mismatched worktree, review worktree, foreign repo) is a leak. `checkEnvLeak` (src/doctor.js) inherits the fix for free since it calls the same function; `preToolHook`/`whichAttempt` (src/hook.js) too.
